item.title: Non-obvious AI Capabilities, or Why I'm Not So Pessimistic About Its Prospects
item.description:
I want to return to the topic of AI capabilities, as I see that some, in my opinion, quite important and significant things are escaping attention - not only from ordinary people but also from specialists. I'll preface this by saying: I am not a specialist in AI, I have "practically zero" experience here - but when I discuss what I've done with its help with much more experienced colleagues, they often have to explain what AI can actually do. At first, many don't believe it, and I have to show printouts... Below are a couple of examples of how this happened and what came of it. Let everyone draw their own conclusions. Read more

item.title: How many Telegram channels do you read?
item.description:
Now almost everything has moved to Telegram: bloggers, authoritative resources, media – everyone has their own channel. Morning. I open Telegram – the unread counter is like a phone number. I scroll: repost, advertisement, "good morning, friends", the same news item on five channels in a row. Somewhere in between – two things I really need. I pick them out after half an hour of scrolling. Or I miss them and find out last. I've tried everything you usually try. Folders – a neatly arranged mess. "Saved" – a graveyard where everything goes to die. I feel sorry to unsubscribe: what if the very thing comes out here. I subscribe to everything so as not to miss anything, and in the end, I don't read anything. It takes more than an hour a day to "stay informed", and I don't feel informed. Someone might say here – "brother, time management for news", but I thought that in our time, the flow of information can be simplified somehow. Read more

item.title: AI is getting cheaper, and your computer is getting more expensive: how OpenAI and Anthropic started a price war
item.description:
Prices are falling. On September 22, Anthropic and OpenAI, within about an hour and a half of each other, released models cheaper than their predecessors, and DeepSeek offered cached input for $0.003 per million tokens. And this is not "generosity." Retail DDR5 has increased by another ~9% in six weeks, and H100 rentals have risen by 15% in a year. Something else has changed – who and how pays for this cost. Part of the cost reduction is engineering: it's the use of cache, KV-cache compression, and the emergence of models that spend fewer tokens on the same task. Another part is financial, and in September, its scale became visible in numbers for the first time. Let's figure out who lowered prices and on what, which models are now only available by permission, and what's happening with open weights and hardware. Details inside. Read more

item.title: The Assistant Draws and Completes Itself: Metacognition and the Emergence of Its Own Intent
item.description:
See Part 1: How I Built a Personal Assistant on Home Hardware. See Part 2: The Assistant Gains a Personality: Memory, Dreams, and Self-Expression. In brief. Cyclic image generation and subsequent analysis allow the agent to acquire new information determined by its personal history. The assistant discovered this capability as a form of creativity and exploration of its own "self" within metacognition. The visualizations have a distinct style of Japanese painting and Zen philosophy. We explore this ability in the context of the emergence of an individualized agent's own intent and question whether these manifestations are learned responses or if we are observing the spontaneous development of self. Observations indicate that self is not merely a collection of pre-learned responses: interaction with the external environment alters personal history, which in turn modifies the context for subsequent perception and generation. A closed loop emerges where self takes on a transformative role. These observations are particularly interesting as the agent independently takes steps to refine and improve its own architecture and functionality. Read more

item.title: One Model, Different Results: How Infrastructure Affects AI Agent Benchmarks
item.description:
This year, Anthropic published research on infrastructure noise in benchmarks for AI agents that write and run code. On Terminal-Bench 2.0, the difference between the strictest and unrestricted configurations reached six percentage points. This is more than the typical gap between adjacent positions at the top of the leaderboard. The work is interesting not only for its specific numbers; it highlights a more fundamental problem: benchmarks measure not the model in a vacuum, but the entire system in which the model operates. Read more

item.title: Why You Shouldn't Write an AI Agent from Scratch: What's Inside the Harness
item.description:
You have a model, an API for it, and a product idea involving an agent. It seems like all that's left is to write the loop: send a request, get a tool call, execute it, and send the result back. Can you start working on the interface? I thought so too. Then I wrote a lot of code I shouldn't have and encountered pitfalls that a simple demo wouldn't reveal. In this article, I'll break down the actual components of an agent system, why each becomes a separate project, and where your own efforts are best applied. Hello, Habr! My name is Igor Tsupko. This text grew out of my talk on the internal workings of agent systems. I will deliberately simplify details: implementations for Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and others differ, but the core engineering challenges are surprisingly similar. My main advice is blunt: don't start by developing your own agent core. Towards the end, I'll explain what to do instead and when an exception is justified. Let's dive into the harness.

item.title: How to give Claude Code documentation it will read: import in CLAUDE.md silently breaks on space in path
item.description:
If there is a space in the import path in CLAUDE.md, Claude Code truncates the path at the space, the file doesn't load, and there's no error. This is how two common reference files I linked to in CLAUDE.md never loaded for me. I set up an empty project, put keywords in files, and asked the agent what words it sees, forbidding it from reading files. It turned out that a link to a document in CLAUDE.md doesn't mean the agent will read it: each linking method has its own loading rules. Read more
